about: The user's plaster pieces (10-21). See README.md and docs/real-light-test.md. sunToFlat: the homography taking a pixel of the raw sun photo to the flat crop (tools/realref/register.py, recomputed 10-24; warping with it gives the -lined photo within JPEG noise, 1.7 levels).

door.sun_direction: upper left (shadows inside the recessed dark block), about 135 deg (0 right, 90 up)
door.notes: Elevation and width unknown; measure_sun.cjs was run with 30 deg, 60 cm.

lintel.notes: Elevation from the lintel's shadow (264 px = 0.205 of the panel width); 11.9-13.6 deg if the block sits 1/8-1/4 in lower. The lintel stands off the plaster: its cast shadow is not measurable from shading. deepest_relief_in is lowest to highest: the user (10-24, later) says the plaster goes about 1/8 in below the average surface in the recesses and about 1/8 in above it elsewhere (first read as 1/8 in in all).

band.notes: Outdoors, even daylight; colour (orange band) and a near-black band.

closeup.notes: Already cropped; near-black band: room light alone cannot keep it from crushing (guard).
